Before it became widespread on the internet the lucky people were blissfully ignorant of just how bad police behavior had become versus what you would expect from people who are supposed to be professionals. For the people who never had to suffer discrimination and profiling by police there was a media veil keeping it out of sight. With the proliferation of small portable camera technology it made it nearly impossible for the even the bought-and-paid-for news networks to ignore the sheer volume of killings and brutality going on. Once the major news outlets began to do their token coverage (so as not to appear apathetic to normal people) of high-profile incidents it was like a feedback loop that strengthened citizen's resolve to capture and publish more of this dangerous/deadly behavior that has been going on out of the spotlight for decades.

The danger of being murdered by a cop at practically any time is REAL. If we want that to change then we can't just ignore it when the front page is swamped with tales of being beaten or killed. Each person has to take it upon themselves to try and determine what is a story worthy of public outrage and what is an unfortunate series of events that someone is trying to sensationalize. Look at everything, and don't jump to conclusions. But don't sweep it under the rug.
